applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8, particularly Building 1 and Building 8 (closest to overhead electric lines on western and southern boundaries)
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) confirms overhead electric utility lines (O.H.U.L.) with utility poles exist along Valley View Road (western boundary) and southern property boundary. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings 1-8 with Building 1 dimensioned at 26.1' and Building 8 at 26.6' from the western property line. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) references existing OHE lines. However, NO building elevation sheets are provided in the 39-sheet set. NO dimension annotations show horizontal clearances from buildings to the outside conductor of overhead lines. NO surveyed conductor elevations are shown on any drawings.
findings.reasoning: While buildings are set back approximately 26+ feet from the property line, the requirement is to maintain a 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the OUTSIDE CONDUCTOR of overhead electric conductors. Without surveyed conductor elevation data, clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to building faces, and no building elevation drawings showing the vertical relationship, it is impossible to verify that the minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained. The code requires clearance measured from the outside conductor (which may be offset several feet from the pole center on multi-conductor installations), not from the pole or property line. Applicant has acknowledged responsibility for maintaining clearances (Sheet 3, Block 8), but has not provided the necessary documentation to demonstrate compliance.
findings.comment: Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor locations and clearance dimensions are required to demonstrate that buildings maintain minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines. No such documentation is present on the site plan.

applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8 in relation to distribution primary and neutral conductors on western and southern boundaries
findings.observation: Sheets 4, 9, and 21 confirm existing overhead electric (O.H.U.L.) facilities adjacent to the property. However, the conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) are not labeled or identified on any plans. The 15-foot radial clearance requirement applies specifically to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. No dimension annotations show radial clearances from any building or customer facility to these conductors. No plan notes identify whether the existing lines are distribution (voltage <60kV) or transmission (voltage ≥60kV), and no conductor types are labeled.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires customer facilities (including buildings) to maintain 15-foot radial clearance from the OUTSIDE CONDUCTOR of distribution primary and neutral conductors. Without identification of conductor types and without dimension annotations showing radial clearances from buildings to the conductors, compliance cannot be verified. The 15-foot clearance measurement requires identification of which conductors are primary/neutral vs. secondary, and this distinction is absent from the plans.
findings.comment: Plan documentation required: (1) identification of existing conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) on overhead lines; (2) dimension annotations showing minimum 15-foot radial clearance from buildings and other customer facilities to the outside conductor of distribution primary and neutral conductors; (3) clarification of whether existing lines are distribution or transmission voltage.

applicableAreas: Building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, roofs) for Buildings 1-8
findings.observation: Site Plan (Sheet 9) shows buildings 1-8 with footprints and general layout, but no section views or elevation drawings depicting building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, roofs, patios) relative to overhead electric conductors. No surveyed conductor elevations are provided. Building architectural details or elevations showing projection dimensions are not included in the 39-sheet set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires building projections to maintain both (1) 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and (2) 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductors. Without section views or elevation drawings showing the vertical and horizontal relationships between building projections and the overhead conductors, and without surveyed conductor elevation data, compliance with these requirements cannot be verified. Buildings can only be shown in plan view without cross-sections showing their height relative to conductor height.
findings.comment: Building elevation or section exhibits are required showing all projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, canopies) with dimension lines from the surveyed outside conductor location to the outermost edges of projections, demonstrating both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances.

applicableAreas: Buildings 1, 2, 8 adjacent to Valley View Road right-of-way where overhead electric facilities are located
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows overhead utility lines and utility poles along Valley View Road (western boundary). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings 1, 2, and 8 positioned near the western property line adjacent to Valley View Road ROW. Building 1 is dimensioned at 26.1' from the western property line; Building 8 at 26.6'. However, NO surveyed conductor elevation data is shown, NO dimension annotations show clearances from buildings to the outside conductor, and NO section views demonstrate that permanent 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances are maintained from electric facilities in the adjacent ROW.
findings.reasoning: No surveyed elevation data or clearance dimensions provided showing that buildings adjacent to Valley View Road maintain required permanent clearances from outside conductor of overhead electric facilities in ROW. Proximity survey data by registered surveyor is needed.
findings.comment: Surveyed elevations of overhead conductors with clearance dimension annotations from the outside conductor to building faces are required, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radial clearance from electric facilities in the adjacent Valley View Road right-of-way.

applicableAreas: All buildings proposed within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: The 39-sheet site plan set does not include any building elevation sheets. Sheet 9 shows building footprints and FFEs but is a plan view only. The README index lists sheets 1-39 with the following titles: Sheets 1-11 are general plans; Sheets 12-20 are utility and drainage plans; Sheets 21-39 are details and landscape plans. NO sheets titled 'Building Elevations,' 'Building Elevation Sheets,' or similar are listed. Consequently, surveyed overhead conductor elevations and clearance dimension annotations are not present on any elevation sheets.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 explicitly requires surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors to be included on building elevation sheets to demonstrate required clearances are met. The absence of building elevation sheets constitutes a failure to provide the required documentation. The code requirement is specific: 'Surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors not included on building elevation sheets to demonstrate required clearances are met' is identified as a deficiency.
findings.comment: Building elevation sheets prepared by the architect/engineer are required, showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations with clearance dimension annotations from the conductor to building faces, roofs, parapets, and all projections, for all buildings within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities.

applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8 and retaining walls adjacent to overhead electric lines
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings in plan view only with no section line callouts (A-A, B-B, etc.) that would reference section views showing clearances. Sheet 22 shows standard construction details for curbs, sidewalks, and driveways but contains no section views specifically showing clearances from outer electric conductor to building edges. Sheets 38-39 show wall construction details and sections but not clearance dimensions from overhead conductors to wall faces. Examined sheets do not include section or plan view exhibits with dimension lines originating at the outer electric conductor and extending to building edges or wall faces.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires 'Section and plan view exhibits [that] show dimensions from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of buildings and building projections for clearance verification.' This is a specific documentation requirement. The absence of any section views with dimension lines from the outer conductor to building edges or wall faces constitutes non-compliance. The requirement applies when buildings or structures are proposed within potential clearance distance, which is the case here.
findings.comment: Provide section view exhibits (with title callouts such as Section A-A, B-B) on site plan or separate detail sheets showing dimension lines from the surveyed outside conductor location to the outermost edges of each building and all building projections, clearly labeling clearances in feet and inches.

applicableAreas: Retaining walls, particularly along southern property boundary where OHE line is located
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows retaining walls labeled 'Begin Concrete Retaining Wall' along the southern boundary and other site perimeter locations. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions) shows an overhead electric line (O.H.U.L.) running along the southern property boundary. Sheets 38-39 (Wall Plans) provide wall construction sections showing max 14-foot height, reinforcement details, and structural dimensions, but contain NO sections showing clearance dimensions from the overhead electric conductor to the wall face or top. Wall plan sheets show only structural reinforcement and soil pressure calculations, not clearances to adjacent overhead lines.
findings.reasoning: The requirement under UCM § 1.10.3 is to maintain a minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines. Retaining walls up to 14 feet tall are proposed along the southern boundary where overhead electric lines are present. Without section views showing the surveyed conductor elevation and the distance (measured horizontally at ground level) from the conductor to the wall face, compliance cannot be verified. The wall height is known (up to 14 feet from foundation), but the conductor height and horizontal distance from the conductor to the wall are not documented.
findings.comment: Provide section views of retaining walls showing the surveyed overhead conductor elevation and clearance dimensions (measured horizontally) from the outside conductor location to the near face of the retaining wall, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance.

applicableAreas: Retaining walls adjacent to overhead electric facilities on southern and eastern boundaries
findings.observation: Sheets 38-39 (Wall Plans and Wall Details) contain section views of retaining walls showing structural reinforcement, backfill requirements, footing details, and maximum heights (14 feet). However, these section views show only internal wall construction and soil pressure relationships. NO section views include dimension lines showing clearance from an outer electric conductor to the outermost edge (top or face) of the retaining wall. Sheet 9 shows OHE line along southern boundary, but Sheets 38-39 do not cross-reference or show the conductor on their wall sections.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 specifically requires 'Retaining walls lack section exhibits showing dimensions from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of wall for clearance verification' to be addressed. This is an explicit documentation requirement. The wall construction sections present on Sheets 38-39 do not show the overhead conductor location or clearance dimensions from the conductor to the wall. The requirement is for section exhibits that include both the wall profile AND the conductor location with a dimensioned clearance.
findings.comment: Provide section view exhibits of each retaining wall showing the surveyed outside conductor location with dimension lines to the outermost edge (top/face) of the wall, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance from the conductor to the wall.

applicableAreas: Proposed driveways crossing or passing under or adjacent to overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows driveways marked 'Construct Type II Driveway' and 'Construct Type III Driveway' on the western and internal portions of the site. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows existing and proposed contours with driveway grades and spot elevations, but contains NO profile sections showing the vertical clearance from lowest point of overhead conductors (including any attached telecommunications lines) to the driveway surface. Sheet 22 shows standard driveway construction details (thickness, reinforcement, grades) but NO sections showing vertical clearance to overhead lines. The FFE elevations of buildings are provided (ranging from 683' to 687.5' NAVD 88), but overhead conductor elevations are not given.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires driveways to maintain minimum 16-foot vertical clearance (for parking without truck traffic) or 18-foot vertical clearance (for areas with truck traffic) from the lowest point of overhead electric facilities including telecommunications attachments. This requires (1) surveyed conductor height data, (2) profile or section views showing clearance calculations, and (3) mid-span clearance verification if the clearance appears marginal. None of these are provided. Applicant has not verified mid-span clearances with registered surveyor data, and no vertical clearance dimensions are shown on grading or profile sheets.
findings.comment: Provide grading profile sections for proposed driveways showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations at the low point and dimension annotations verifying minimum 16-foot or 18-foot vertical clearance (depending on truck traffic designation) from the lowest point of all overhead conductors and attached equipment to the finished driveway surface.

applicableAreas: Vehicle parking and display areas beneath overhead electric lines
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows 10 surface parking spaces and 78 garage parking spaces for a total of 88 spaces (per site plan data table). The parking layout is shown on the plan view, but NO section views show vertical clearance dimensions from overhead electric lines to the parking surface. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows parking pad elevations and site topography but does not provide surveyed conductor heights or clearance verification. No note on site plan indicates the vertical clearance requirement or that parking must maintain minimum clearance from overhead lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires parking areas to maintain minimum vertical clearance from overhead electric lines (12 feet for residential pedestrian areas, 16 feet for parking without trucks, 18 feet with truck traffic). Without surveyed conductor elevations and section views showing the vertical relationship between parking pads and conductors, compliance cannot be verified. Additionally, a site plan note is required indicating the clearance requirement. No such note is present on Sheets 9 or 11.
findings.comment: Provide section views of parking areas with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and dimension annotations verifying minimum vertical clearance (16 feet for parking without truck traffic, or 18 feet for areas with truck traffic) from lowest point of conductors to finished parking surface. Add note to site plan specifying clearance requirement and designation of parking areas (truck vs. non-truck traffic).

applicableAreas: All proposed site features and infrastructure
findings.observation: Complete review of Sheets 9 (Site Plan), 11 (Grading Plan), and 21 (Electrical Plan) reveals NO dimension annotations showing clearances from buildings, structures, driveways, walls, or other site features to overhead electric lines. The only distances shown are from property lines and internal site features to each other. Sheet 4 shows the existing utility poles with symbols but no dimension annotations from the poles. No dimension lines on any sheet are shown extending from an identified 'outside conductor' location to site features. Applicant has not labeled the location of outside conductors or the measurement reference point for any clearance annotations.
findings.reasoning: All clearance dimensions (or lack thereof) must be measured from the outside conductor, not from pole center or pole structure. No clearance dimensions are provided on the plans at all, and no plans identify the location of the outside conductor for measurement purposes.
findings.comment: All clearance annotations must be revised to show dimension lines originating at the surveyed outside conductor location (not pole center), with clear identification of which conductor is being measured from, and dimension values showing clearances in feet and inches from the conductor to site features.

applicableAreas: Sidewalks along Valley View Road at property limits
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows utility poles along Valley View Road adjacent to the property. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a proposed '5' Concrete Sidewalk' labeled 'Construct 5' Concrete Sidewalk' in the sidewalk easement area along the western property boundary adjacent to Valley View Road. However, Sheet 9 provides NO dimension annotations showing the alignment of the proposed sidewalk relative to the existing utility poles. The sidewalk alignment appears to follow the property line, but the exact horizontal distance from poles is not dimensioned. Sheet 22 shows standard sidewalk construction details but contains no site-specific dimension relating the sidewalk to pole locations.
findings.reasoning: The requirement under Reviewer Convention is that sidewalks must be 'cleared from existing power poles at each end of property along right-of-way.' This implies that the sidewalk should not conflict with or be immediately adjacent to pole locations at property corners. Without dimension annotations showing the distance from the proposed sidewalk to existing pole locations at the northwest and southwest property corners where the property meets Valley View Road, compliance cannot be verified. The vision analysis of Sheet 9 noted an 'AT&T Pole' at the northwest corner, suggesting a utility pole exists at or near that location.
findings.comment: Provide dimension annotations on site plan showing clearance distance from proposed sidewalk alignment to existing power poles at each end of the property along Valley View Road right-of-way frontage. Confirm sidewalk clearance from pole locations, particularly at northwest and southwest property corners.

applicableAreas: All proposed customer facilities, building structures, and site features relative to existing electric easements and overhead distribution facilities
findings.observation: Facts.md identifies two perpetual easements with NO development permitted: (1) Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731, 0.31 acres) in NE interior—explicitly marked as 'strict no-build zone'; (2) City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137, 0.130 acres) in NE corner with unlimited City access rights. Both are NOT depicted on the submitted site plan (facts.md: 'NOT depicted on the submitted site plan and NOT in the COA GIS easement layer'). Additionally, a 5' Electric Easement (×2) and 7.5' Public Utility Easement are plat-dedicated per facts.md but locations relative to proposed improvements are not verified on site plans. Sheet 2 (Plat) should show all easements, but facts.md notes these are not shown. Sheet 9 shows the general site layout and street easements, but does not clearly depict all recorded electric easement boundaries or verify that proposed features maintain adequate clearance from easement areas.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 contains an absolute prohibition: 'customer facilities proposed to be installed under or over Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities' is prohibited 'regardless of clearance distances.' Additionally, items within electric easements must maintain minimum 7.5-foot clearance from the outside conductor. The facts.md documentation reveals that critical easements (Greenbelt, Drainage, Electric, PUE) are either not depicted or not verified on the site plan. Without accurate easement boundaries shown on plans, applicant cannot demonstrate that (1) no facilities are placed under/over overhead distribution lines in violation of the absolute prohibition, or (2) items within easements maintain required 7.5-foot clearances. A proximity survey by registered surveyor is required to confirm easement boundaries and facility compliance.
findings.comment: Provide comprehensive easement exhibit on site plan showing all recorded easements (Greenbelt Access, City Drainage, 5' Electric Easements ×2, 7.5' Public Utility Easement, and any others per county records) with accurate boundary dimensions. Provide registered surveyor proximity survey confirming: (1) no customer facilities are located under or over overhead distribution lines (absolute prohibition); (2) all facilities within electric easement boundaries maintain minimum 7.5-foot clearance from outside conductor; (3) all facilities comply with easement use restrictions.

applicableAreas: All proposed driveways, parking areas, buildings, and site features with potential vertical clearance concerns from overhead electric lines
findings.observation: Overhead electric lines (O.H.U.L.) are shown on existing survey (Sheet 4) and electrical plan (Sheet 21) but NO surveyed conductor elevation data is provided anywhere on the 39-sheet site plan set. Buildings have FFEs ranging from 683' to 687.5' (Sheet 9, 11), but overhead conductor heights are not documented. Driveways and parking pads have grading elevations shown (Sheet 11), but no profile sections with surveyed mid-span clearance data verify vertical clearances meet requirements. The vision analysis of Sheet 9 noted that buildings are approximately 26-30 feet horizontally from overhead lines on the western boundary—this distance is close enough that vertical clearance verification (mid-span clearance) should be provided per UCM § 1.10.3 guidance for situations where 'clearance appears marginal or insufficient.' No registered surveyor data confirming mid-span clearance is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires 'survey by registered surveyor showing pole locations and mid-span clearances not provided when existing overhead facilities may not meet minimum vertical clearance requirements.' The grouping guidance states that when vertical clearance 'appears marginal or insufficient based on site plan data,' registered surveyor mid-span clearance data is required. The site plan does not provide surveyed conductor elevations, making it impossible to calculate vertical clearances from building FFEs and driveway grades to conductor height. Furthermore, the presence of structures within approximately 26-30 feet horizontally of overhead lines, combined with the absence of conducted elevator data, suggests that clearance verification is required but not provided. This is a deficiency: applicant has failed to provide surveyor data for mid-span clearances.
findings.comment: Provide registered surveyor field survey data documenting: (1) surveyed elevations of overhead electric conductors at mid-span locations above buildings, driveways, and parking areas; (2) calculated vertical clearances from the lowest point of conductors (including attachments) to the highest points of buildings, roof projections, driveways, and parking surfaces, demonstrating compliance with minimum clearance thresholds (7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground for buildings, 16-18 feet for driveways/parking, others as applicable); (3) marked survey points and elevation measurements with registered surveyor certification.

applicableAreas: Proposed exterior lighting fixtures throughout the site
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan, Block 2) includes a 'Lighting Note' requiring all exterior lighting to be 'full cut-off and fully shielded in compliance with Subchapter E 2.5' and providing 'Figure 34: Examples of Fully-Shielded Light Fixtures.' This addresses design standards for light shielding but does NOT address clearances from overhead electric lines. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows the site layout with various landscape elements but does not include dimension annotations showing horizontal or vertical clearances from proposed light fixtures to overhead electric lines. No site plan contains a photometric plan or detailed lighting plan showing fixture locations with clearance dimensions.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires decorative lighting proposed under existing overhead electric lines to meet clearance requirements (7.5-foot sky-to-ground horizontal, 15-foot radial) or be relocated. The site plan shows a general requirement for 'full cut-off' lighting compliance but does not identify where exterior lighting fixtures will be located or provide clearance verification from overhead conductors. Without a detailed lighting plan showing fixture locations and without clearance dimensions from conductors, compliance cannot be verified. If lighting is proposed beneath or within 15 feet of overhead conductors, relocation or clearance documentation is required.
findings.comment: Provide detailed photometric plan or lighting layout showing all proposed exterior and decorative light fixture locations with: (1) horizontal and vertical clearance dimensions from surveyed outside conductor locations; (2) confirmation that fixtures maintain minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances, OR; (3) relocation notes if fixtures cannot meet clearance requirements. Include note on site plan indicating clearance requirement for lighting.

applicableAreas: Tree plantings on landscape plan, particularly within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors or 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan, guide.md) explicitly states: 'Block 2: drawing — Main Landscape and Site Plan. A comprehensive site plan illustrating building footprints, parking layouts, sidewalks, utility lines (Water, Storm Drain, Overhead Electric), topographical contours, and the distribution of landscape elements.' This confirms overhead electric lines are shown on the landscape plan. The sheet index shows Sheets 30-35, 37 address trees and landscaping. However, NO dimension annotations or notes on the landscape plan specify which species are planted within 10 feet of distribution or 50 feet of transmission conductors, and no reference is made to ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible Shade Trees list ('UC'-designated species). Without specific callouts showing tree locations relative to overhead conductors and without verification of species against the UC list, compliance cannot be confirmed. Trees exceeding the utility-compatible size/species may be planted in violation of clearance and future maintenance conflicts with the electric utility.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 specifies a 50-lateral-foot clearance requirement for trees near transmission lines (more restrictive than the 30-40 feet mentioned in ECM § 2.4.1.D/2.4.2.C). Trees within these clearance zones must be from the Utility Compatible list (ECM Appendix F, marked 'UC', generally mature height ≤20 feet). The landscape plan shows tree plantings and site grading but provides NO verification that trees within 10 feet of distribution or 50 feet of transmission conductors are utility-compatible species. Additionally, Sheet 3, Block 8 requires that 'owner shall be responsible for any initial tree pruning and tree removal that is within ten feet of the center line of the proposed overhead electric facilities.' This suggests applicant acknowledges trees are a concern, but the landscape plan does not address compatibility.
findings.comment: Landscape plan must identify all trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors and 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors, verify that species match ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible Shade Trees list ('UC'-designated trees with mature height ≤20 feet), and include note requiring property owner responsibility for ongoing tree pruning/removal within 10 feet of centerline of overhead electric facilities per Austin Energy standard practice and Block 8 requirements.

applicableAreas: Proposed accessible paths, driveways, and site features relative to down guy wires from existing utility poles
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows a 'GUY ANCHOR' symbol (per the legend) at one of the utility poles along Valley View Road, indicating down guy wires are present on the existing utility infrastructure. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the general site layout with driveways, sidewalks, and pedestrian paths, but does NOT depict existing guy wire locations or down guy anchor points. The survey shows the guy anchor exists, but its location relative to the proposed driveways and accessible paths is not dimensioned or verified on Sheet 9. Without down guy wire locations being shown on the site plan and without verification that proposed accessible routes, driveways, or site features do not conflict with guy anchors and cables, compliance cannot be confirmed.
findings.reasoning: Down guy wires are support cables from distribution utility poles to ground anchors. They represent a potential obstruction and conflict risk if proposed accessible paths, driveways, or site features are routed over or through the guy anchor zone. UCM § 1.17.0 (Glossary) defines 'Down Guy' as a distinct feature. The grouping guidance notes that electric utility infrastructure (poles, guy wires, guys) is 'frequently omitted from plans,' suggesting this is a common deficiency. Sheet 4 confirms a guy anchor exists, but Sheet 9 does not show where it is located in relation to proposed site features. If the guy anchor conflicts with proposed improvements, the code requires either (1) pole relocation, or (2) conversion to self-supporting steel poles. The applicant has not addressed this possibility.
findings.comment: Clearly depict on site plan the location of existing down guy wire anchor points shown on the existing survey (Sheet 4). Verify that proposed driveways, accessible paths, parking areas, and other site features do not conflict with guy anchors or guy wire cables. If conflicts exist, provide notes addressing resolution through pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting steel poles per utility company standards.

applicableAreas: Down guy anchor points from existing utility poles
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows a guy anchor symbol at one of the utility poles along Valley View Road. Sheet 2 (Plat) should show easement boundaries, but facts.md indicates that critical easements are not depicted on the submitted site plan. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not show or reference down guy anchor easement boundaries. The grouping guidance specifies that down guy anchor easement requirements are: '10 feet wide extending 5 feet past where down guy enters ground' (per Austin Energy Transmission Engineering Standards). Without easement boundaries shown on the plat or site plan, and without dimension annotations confirming the 10-foot width and 5-foot extension, compliance cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: According to Reviewer Convention and Austin Energy standards, down guy anchor points require dedicated easements to ensure access for maintenance, replacement, and inspection. The required easement is 10 feet wide with minimum 5-foot extension beyond the anchor ground entry point. The existing survey (Sheet 4) confirms a guy anchor exists, but the plat (Sheet 2) and site plan (Sheet 9) do not show or reference the dedicated easement for this anchor. Without easement boundaries shown and dimensioned, applicant has not demonstrated that required easement space is provided and protected from development impacts (buildings, paving, landscaping, etc.).
findings.comment: Depict on site plan and plat all down guy anchor easement boundaries for existing utility poles, showing 10-foot easement width extending minimum 5 feet past the point where the guy wire enters the ground. Verify that proposed site features (buildings, driveways, sidewalks, landscaping) do not encroach on or obstruct the down guy anchor easement area.

applicableAreas: Transformer pads proposed on site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows multiple transformer pad locations throughout the site (labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' at several locations). However, the electrical plan is a plan view showing horizontal placement only. NO section views or elevation drawings accompany the electrical plan showing the vertical relationship between transformer pad height and the surveyed elevation of overhead electric conductors above the site. No vertical clearance dimension annotations are present. Overhead electric lines are shown on the plan as existing 'OHE' lines on the western and southern boundaries, but no section showing the clearance from these conductors to the tops of transformer pads is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires transformers (whether pole-mounted or pad-mounted) to maintain minimum 7.5-foot vertical sky-to-ground clearance from overhead electric lines. This is a vertical clearance requirement, requiring knowledge of both the transformer height and the conductor height. The electrical plan shows transformer pad locations but does not provide the surveyed conductor elevation or section views demonstrating that the 7.5-foot clearance is maintained. This is particularly important if any transformers are located beneath existing overhead lines or where overhead conductors pass over transformer equipment.
findings.comment: Provide section views of proposed transformer pads showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations and dimension annotations verifying minimum 7.5-foot vertical clearance from the lowest point of overhead conductors to the highest point of transformer equipment. If transformers are located beneath existing overhead lines, provide specific clearance verification or relocation notes.

applicableAreas: Construction staging areas, material storage zones, and equipment laydown areas throughout the site
findings.observation: Sheet 5 (Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan) addresses temporary erosion control measures and construction sequencing but does not include a detailed construction staging plan or equipment layout plan showing staging areas, equipment zones, crane swing radius, or material storage locations in relation to overhead electric lines. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the general site development layout but does not designate specific construction staging areas or address 10-foot radial clearances during construction. NO plans address OSHA and UCM § 1.10.2 requirements for 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead lines during construction activities. The sheet list shows no separate 'Construction Phasing Plan' or 'Construction Staging Plan' sheet.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.2 references OSHA 1910.333 and Texas law requirements for construction working clearances. The grouping guidance states: 'Minimum 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead lines (OSHA 1910.333, UCM § 1.10.2) [for] construction working clearances.' This is a mandatory safety requirement during construction and is distinct from permanent clearances. Additionally, the grouping notes: 'OSHA requires a 20-foot clearance from energized transmission lines during construction.' The plans do not demonstrate that construction staging areas, equipment operation zones, crane swing radius, or work platforms will maintain required clearances from overhead energized lines. This is a deficiency: applicant has failed to provide a construction staging/logistics plan addressing these safety clearances.
findings.comment: Provide construction staging/logistics plan (or site phasing plan) showing: (1) all proposed equipment staging areas, material storage zones, and laydown areas; (2) 10-foot radial clearance boundaries from overhead distribution lines (marked as exclusion zones); (3) crane swing radius zones with 10-foot radial clearance from energized lines; (4) 20-foot clearance from transmission lines if transmission structures are present; (5) note requiring contractor to maintain clearances and reference to OSHA 1910.333 working clearance requirements.

applicableAreas: Cover sheet and general notes for entire project
findings.observation: Comprehensive review of Sheet 1 (Cover Sheet) and Sheet 3 (General Notes) reveals the following: Sheet 1 contains project title, location map, fire department requirements, environmental notes, various compliance statements, but NO note requiring 48-hour notification to Austin Energy before work begins near overhead lines. Sheet 3, Block 20 includes 'Electric Transmission Notes' (16 items) which specifically require (Item 3): 'A pre-construction safety meeting is required with Austin Energy 48 hours before commencement of construction... OSHA requires a 20' clearance from energized transmission lines during construction.' This note applies specifically to TRANSMISSION facilities and includes a 48-hour requirement for a SAFETY MEETING. However, Sheet 3, Blocks 8/14 ('Electric Notes') address general distribution lines but contain NO requirement for 48-hour notification before construction work begins near distribution overhead lines. Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003, requires notification to utilities before work on high-voltage lines, and UCM § 1.10.2 incorporates this requirement. The plans do not include this general notification requirement for distribution lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.2 explicitly requires a plan note: 'Plans must include note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines (Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003).' While Sheet 3, Block 20 requires a 48-hour pre-construction safety MEETING for transmission lines specifically, there is NO corresponding note for general construction notification before work begins near distribution overhead lines. This is a regulatory and safety requirement distinct from the transmission-specific safety meeting. The note is required to be on the cover sheet or in the general notes to inform owner, contractor, and City of the notification requirement.
findings.comment: Add note to cover sheet (Sheet 1) or general notes (Sheet 3) stating: 'Owner and contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before beginning any work, excavation, or construction activities within or adjacent to areas containing overhead electric facilities and lines. Notification is required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003, and UCM § 1.10.2. Contact information: [Austin Energy contact details]. Failure to notify may result in serious injury, fatality, or project delays.'
